title: the scratch scan reads a temp call held in a string as a reach only where the string runs
intention: bare_temp_reach names a mkdtemp or gettempdir held in a string only where the string, or a name bound to it, reaches a call that runs text or writes it where it can be run, so a command a gate only judges reads as data and a child script's text still reads as a reach.
why: Measured 2026-11-23 on akiendelllinux (cairn e0c2b62ac): bare_temp_reach named bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py:187, a measured shell command held in a string. Its one consumer is `for command in measured: assert gate.verdict(command) is None` (:193), and bin/cmd/deletegate has no subprocess, exec, eval, Popen or os.system call site. So it is data the delete gate judges, not a reach, yet it reds scratch's corpus tooth and bin's own (red tickets 0746da231128, a30a49e8631f, e3b9eef2fc1e). The scan reads strings on purpose: 008baf08f4d8's reach was a child script's text (248a29f29^, the git-env proof line 46), written with write_text and run with subprocess. The file test_delete_gate.py does call subprocess (:286-305, the gate run on a JSON payload), so a per-file 'has a sink' rule cannot tell the two apart; the rule must follow each string.
traces_to: Law 9 (a red from a scan reading data as a reach is distance from no spec, and it blocks every component the corpus tooth reads) and Law 4 (the door stays physics: the reach the scan was built for, 008baf08f4d8's, is still named).
how: In bare_temp_reach, parse each proof; a string holding a temp word whose value reaches no sink call (exec, eval, compile, os.system/popen, subprocess.*, run/call, write/write_text/write_bytes, a local function that calls one) has its span marked data, and a hit inside a data span is not named. Flow is followed up through expressions, across names bound by assignment, for targets and returns; a binding it cannot follow counts as running. Text outside strings counts as before; an unparseable file reads line by line as before. Built on akienasus/b563-scan-sink-flow (d9909fce1).

clauses.claim: over one fixture proof, bare_temp_reach names exactly the string written to a file that is run, the string handed to subprocess, and the bare call, and names neither the measured command a judge only reads, the assert message nor the docstring

decisions.text: D1: cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py bare_temp_reach marks the spans of strings that reach no running call as data (_data_string_spans, _runs, _bound_runs); its docstring says so.

D2: cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_scratch.py gains test_bare_temp_reach_names_a_string_only_where_it_runs, PROVES b563bf636e5d key '1', exact equality over a 17-line fixture, inside the control-group file the corpus tooth already exempts.

out: every component's own scratch-door tooth (0d98f7325181, f5859eae9e08 carry theirs)
